questions.prompt: Which practice best supports reliable work with stored procedures?
options: Assume the database engines behave identically.
Skip edge-case checks because the sample returns rows.
Document side effects and engine-specific procedural behavior.
Add unrelated clauses until the output looks plausible.
questions.answer_key: Document side effects and engine-specific procedural behavior.
questions.explanation: Document side effects and engine-specific procedural behavior. The lesson keeps the distinction between core SQL concepts and engine-specific behavior explicit.

questions.prompt: When an example related to stored procedures produces an unexpected result, what should you do first?
options: Assume every SQL engine applies identical rules.
Inspect a small result, test a boundary or missing-value case, and compare it with the documented behavior.
Run the same statement repeatedly without inspecting the data.
Remove constraints and access controls until the query succeeds.
questions.answer_key: Inspect a small result, test a boundary or missing-value case, and compare it with the documented behavior.
questions.explanation: A small, controlled test makes query behavior explainable. Inspect the data shape, conditions, NULLs, ties, plan, or transaction state that applies to the specific topic.
